solutions.latex:
Possible points of inflexion: $f''(x)=0$

$6x^2 - 36x + 40 = 0$

$x = \dfrac{36 \pm \sqrt{(-36)^2 - 4(6)(40)}}{12} = \dfrac{36 \pm 4\sqrt{21}}{12} = \dfrac{9 \pm \sqrt{21}}{3}$

Testing for change in concavity:

$$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} x & 0 & \frac{9-\sqrt{21}}{3} & 3 & \frac{9+\sqrt{21}}{3} & 6 \\ \hline f''(x) & 40 & 0 & -14 & 0 & 40 \end{array}$$

As there is a change in concavity, there are points of inflexion at $x = \dfrac{9+\sqrt{21}}{3}$ and $x = \dfrac{9-\sqrt{21}}{3}$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct x co-ordinates; 1: correctly tests for points of inflexion
1: correct shape; 1: correct stationary points; 1: correct points of inflexion

solutions.latex:
At $P = 1500$, $t = 15$: $1500 = 40500\,b^{-\frac{15}{5}}$

$\dfrac{1}{27} = b^{-3}$, so $27 = b^3$, $b = 3$

Want $t$ when $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = -25$.

$P = 40500 \times 3^{-\frac{t}{5}}$ (using $y = a^x$, $y' = \ln a \times a^x$)

$\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 40500 \times \dfrac{-1}{5}\ln 3 \times 3^{-\frac{t}{5}} = -8100\ln 3 \times 3^{-\frac{t}{5}} = -25$

$3^{-\frac{t}{5}} = \dfrac{1}{324\ln 3}$

$-\dfrac{t}{5} = \dfrac{\ln\left(\frac{1}{324\ln 3}\right)}{\ln 3}$

$t = \dfrac{-5\ln\left(\frac{1}{324\ln 3}\right)}{\ln 3} = 26.737\ldots \approx 26.7$ years
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: b = 3; 1: wants dP/dt = -25; 1: correct derivative; 1: t = 26.7 years

solutions.latex:
$V = \pi r^2 h$, $V = 380$, so $380 = \pi r^2 h$ and $h = \dfrac{380}{\pi r^2}$

$A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r\left(\dfrac{380}{\pi r^2}\right) = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{760\pi r}{\pi r^2}$

$A = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{760}{r}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct expression for h; 1: substitutes and simplifies to the required result

solutions.latex:
$\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 4\pi r - \dfrac{760}{r^2}$

$\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2} = 4\pi + \dfrac{1520}{r^3}$

$r > 0$, so $\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2} > 0$, therefore a minimum value.

Minimum occurs when $\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 0$: $4\pi r - \dfrac{760}{r^2} = 0$, so $4\pi r^3 = 760$, $r^3 = \dfrac{760}{4\pi}$, $r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{760}{4\pi}} \doteq 3.925$ m
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct first derivative; 1: shows minimum using second derivative; 1: correct value of r

solutions.latex:
Stationary point when $f'(x) = 0$: $\ln x = -1$, so $x = \dfrac{1}{e}$ or $e^{-1}$

$f(e^{-1}) = \dfrac{1}{e}\ln e^{-1} = -\dfrac{1}{e}$ or $-e^{-1}$

$f''(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}$, domain $x > 0$, so $f''(x) > 0$

Therefore $(e^{-1}, -e^{-1})$ is a minimum.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: shows one stationary point; 1: determines nature (minimum)
